_readme: The KPI registry. This file decides what the city measures and where each
measurement stands on a property hex. Everything else — the importer, the
HTTP ingest endpoint, the roster, the legend — reads it.
PARCEL NUMBERS ARE PERMANENT. Position 10 is signage on every property,
forever. Renumbering would move every object on every hex and destroy the
layout you had learned to read. To add a KPI, take the next vacant number;
never reuse or shuffle one. 01 is the centre landmark and belongs to no KPI.
KIND decides how a reading becomes a pillar height:
variance  money. value = budget - actual, so NEGATIVE is overspent and bad.
Scaled against the 90th percentile of its own unfavourable
readings, so payroll dollars and fuel dollars stay comparable.
ratio     value out of total (screens online out of screens installed).
Height is the shortfall against target. total 0 = nothing here.
count     value against target, with direction at-least or at-most.
boolean   done or not done.
label     text about the property, not a reading. No parcel, no pillar —
it shows up on the roster and the detail card.
CADENCE sets how long a reading stays believable: realtime 1 day, daily 3,
weekly 10, monthly 45, quarterly 120. Past that the parcel goes back to
'no data' rather than showing a stale value, because a feed that quietly
died is the failure mode this whole map exists to catch.
CEILING caps a KPI below full height. The automotive lines are real but
secondary; without a cap a few hundred dollars of fuel out-shouts a
five-figure payroll overrun.
TARGETS marked PLACEHOLDER below are guesses. Set them to your real
standards before trusting the colours.
